key_insight: VideoMaMa++ proposes a preserve-and-refine token to make video matting more temporally consistent across separately processed chunks. The goal is to prevent foreground transparency and boundaries from changing abruptly between chunks.
problem_solved: Compute-heavy video diffusion models typically process only 6–24 frames at a time. Matting each chunk independently from coarse mask guidance can produce inconsistent results across chunk boundaries.
method: Build on diffusion-based video matting, which uses pretrained video priors to generalize from limited synthetic training data.
Introduce a preserve-and-refine token to address cross-chunk consistency, as indicated by the paper title; the supplied abstract is truncated before implementation details.
impact: More consistent matting could improve foreground extraction and video compositing over longer clips. The supplied excerpt does not establish measured quality gains or inference-cost changes.
visual_elements: A video timeline split into 6–24-frame chunks, with chunk boundaries highlighted.
Side-by-side foreground matte sequences illustrating inconsistent versus temporally stable edges.
A conceptual preserve-and-refine token linking adjacent video chunks.
A pipeline diagram: video and coarse masks → diffusion-based matting → foreground alpha mattes.
paper_title: VideoMaMa++: Temporally Consistent Video Matting via Preserve-and-Refine Token
paper_authors: Sangbeom Lim, Seoung Wug Oh, Heeji Yoon, Seungryong Kim, Joon-Young Lee
